question_text: A 75-year-old woman presents to the emergency department because of a brief loss of consciousness, slurred speech, and facial numbness. Family members report that she complained about feeling chest pain and shortness of breath while on her morning walk. Medical history is noncontributory. Physical examination shows decreased pupil reactivity to light and hemiplegic gait. Her pulse is 120/min, respirations are 26/min, temperature is 36.7°C (98.0°F), and blood pressure is 160/80 mm Hg. On heart auscultation, S1 is loud, widely split, and there is a diastolic murmur. Transthoracic echocardiography in a 4-chamber apical view revealed a large oval-shaped and sessile left atrial mass. Which of the following is the most likely complication of this patient's condition?
